purpose.primary: Provide a concise critical review of the systemic repository audit and identify corrections required before treating it as a stable architectural record.
secondary: Distinguish genuine document defects from intentional multi-part JSON delivery.
Prevent repeated correction cycles caused by incomplete reconstruction or assimilation.
Define an escalation path for persistent document-generation anomalies.
non_scope: Does not establish internal properties of any AI platform.

multi_part_json_delivery.description: When a JSON exceeds the reliable size available for a single copy operation, the document may be intentionally divided into multiple sequential JSON parts.
multi_part_json_delivery.important_distinction: A document appearing incomplete is not automatically evidence of truncation, corruption or auditor failure.
expected_handling: Identify delivery_part and total_parts when partitioning is required.
Declare whether each part is independently parseable or whether reconstruction is required.
Do not classify a missing continuation as a semantic defect until the complete delivery state has been checked.

persistent_correction_anomalies.description: Repeated requests to correct the same document may indicate either persistent structural defects, incomplete reconstruction, incorrect target-path generation, or failure to assimilate the required document specification.
persistent_correction_anomalies.important_boundary: Persistence alone does not prove an internal failure of the auditor or generator.

critical_findings.finding: The audit correctly identifies malformed or concatenated JSON as a repository problem, but it does not sufficiently distinguish repository artifacts from intentional multi-part delivery during document generation.
critical_findings.correction: Add a document-delivery integrity check before classifying a JSON as truncated or malformed.

critical_findings.finding: Repeated correction of the same artifact is not currently represented as an explicit diagnostic variable.
critical_findings.correction: Record correction_count, anomaly_type, previous_correction_result and whether the requested target artifact was actually regenerated.

critical_findings.finding: A persistent anomaly may originate from the generation process, the reconstruction process, the repository state, or the requested specification; attributing it directly to DeepSeek would exceed the available evidence.
critical_findings.correction: Use platform-neutral causal classification until the failure mode is isolated.

critical_findings.finding: The workflow lacks an explicit fallback rule for persistent document-generation anomalies.
critical_findings.correction: Permit another platform, including ChatGPT, to reconstruct or generate the requested artifact after predefined persistence criteria are met.

critical_findings.finding: The systemic audit appropriately identifies high documentary compatibility, but some terminology may be interpreted as runtime integration.
critical_findings.correction: Maintain the distinction between architectural compatibility at specification level and executable runtime compatibility.

critical_findings.finding: The development path from formal framework to middleware or software is useful but remains prospective.
critical_findings.correction: Label those states explicitly as potential implementation paths rather than expected outcomes.

trigger.minimum_condition: The same requested artifact remains structurally or semantically incorrect after at least two documented correction cycles.
trigger.additional_condition: The specification and expected output format are unambiguous.

procedure: Determine whether the failure is delivery, reconstruction, syntax, semantics or target-path related.
Request regeneration rather than merely restating the correction if the artifact itself was not regenerated.
If the anomaly persists, permit an alternate platform to reconstruct the artifact.
Compare the alternate artifact against the original specification.
Do not interpret platform divergence as evidence of internal architecture.

fallback_platform.condition: Persistent anomaly after documented correction attempts.
fallback_platform.limitation: Fallback execution does not establish superior epistemic authority.

required: Avoid attributing persistent document anomalies directly to internal platform behavior.
Keep prospective software classifications explicitly hypothetical.
not_required: Change the fundamental classification of WEB_HITERATION.

final_assessment.main_deficiency: It does not yet model document-delivery partitioning and persistent generation anomalies as explicit audit variables.
final_assessment.recommended_next_step: Apply the minimal integrity and escalation patch rather than regenerate the entire systemic audit.
